title: Snapshots Aren't Backups: Know the Difference

scenes.say: Snapshots or backups? Which one actually protects your VMs when disaster hits?

scenes.label: Snapshot
scenes.sub: A point-in-time delta on the same storage
scenes.say: A snapshot is just a point-in-time delta, saved on the same datastore as your VM.

scenes.label: Backup
scenes.sub: A separate copy on different storage
scenes.say: A backup is a separate copy, stored on different storage, often offsite or in the cloud.
Snapshots let you roll back a patch fast, but they stay on the same storage and can slow things down. Backups are for real disaster recovery—they live elsewhere and stick around.

scenes.title: Restoring from backup
scenes.say: Restoring from backup means you can recover your VM even if the original datastore is gone.

scenes.question: Are snapshots a backup?
scenes.right: No, snapshots aren't backups. They're just deltas on the same storage and vanish if the datastore fails.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: are snapshots a backup? Nope. If your datastore fails, your snapshots vanish too.
